solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ancient period's character captured by wise person

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
tone as in the character or mood of something

explanation.surface: A historical era whose spirit is preserved by a learned scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' here means mood or quality, not a letter or a person in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric era when tools were made of stone, about as ancient a period as history names.

clue.text: Wonderful fruit at the bottom of U-boat

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, a sub
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A sailor delighted to find fruit stored in the hold of a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the fruit sitting at the bottom of the U-boat means it comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime is an adjective for something so excellent or beautiful it inspires awe.

clue.text: Give a speech, primarily on robbery and tax evasion

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each following word is kept

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A prosecutor addressing a court mainly about theft and dodging tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address, the verb behind oration.

clue.text: See Croat jet crashing? This could be used!

definitions.text: See Croat jet crashing? This could be used!

indicators.note: a crashing plane breaks apart, so the letters before it are smashed into a new order

parts.note: the eleven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot whose Croatian jet is going down would want to escape it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a pilot in a crashing jet would use an ejector seat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector seat fires a pilot clear of a stricken aircraft, exactly what you'd use if the jet were crashing.

clue.text: New lager includes oxygen in abundance

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other
something new is made afresh, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A freshly brewed beer full of bubbles of gas, available in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore is placed after a noun to mean in great quantity, matching the phrase in abundance.

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: to tap a phone is to listen in secretly

explanation.surface: A revolutionary agent bugging a quarrel between others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, a brief argument.

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: Advice to obtain a treatment from a qualified expert.
explanation.definitionFit: To procure is to obtain or acquire something, often with some effort.

clue.text: Country not upset over general assembly at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the words just before it

parts.note: the initials of these two words

explanation.surface: A nation unbothered by what goes on at a United Nations General Assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom in the South Pacific, an island country.

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes, the two end letters of the following word

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A daring fashion choice: letting one's bra show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'extremely visible' as very noticeable; here it means only the ends of 'visible'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and bold are synonyms for showing courage or daring.

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a loon is a foolish person
amp is short for amplifier

explanation.surface: Jeering at an idiot lugging his guitar amp around.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to ridicule them publicly through satire, so it is a verb meaning to mock.

clue.text: Astounding request to a tall person at a concert?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: amazing, boggling the brain

definitions.text: request to a tall person at a concert?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a polite ask, read as 'would you mind stooping down?' to someone blocking the view

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer into two words: 'Mind bending?' is what you might say to a tall person blocking your view on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind-bending describes something so strange or impressive it is hard to take in, so it is a synonym of astounding.

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Cooling a jug of drink on a routine basis.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice something is to chill it, as with a drink put on ice.

indicators.note: scuttling suggests scurrying about in disorder, so the letters are moved around

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A spider is a born scurrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuttling' fits the spider picture so well that it hides its job as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, so it is an example of the definition.

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's partner has had her corset tightened.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a person who accompanies another, a companion.

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a curate is an assistant parish priest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man of the cloth or a gallery head is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link offering two definitions, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the keeper of a museum or gallery collection, in charge of its exhibits.

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word
mailed means posted, sent

explanation.surface: A gardener finally posting a herb to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the definition, though it reads like part of 'mailed out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out is not present, which is what absent means.

indicators.note: arranged means put into order, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Having to pay both the rent and the car's MOT test at once is painful.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the annual roadworthiness test required for older cars in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering of body or mind, a near synonym of agony.

indicators.note: to discard is to throw away, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a skipper is the captain of a boat or team
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A ship's master throwing back the little fish he caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small fish' looks like one phrase, but 'small' is the letter dropped and 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a split, salted and smoked herring, so it is a kind of fish.

indicators.note: somehow says the result is reached by some unstated means, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Somehow getting hold of a Nordic orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is one of the Scandinavian countries, so Norwegian is an example of from Scandinavia.

clue.text: Writer heads north over a large country

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means going upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An author travelling north across a big nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author; here it is the thing a writer uses. 'over' places that piece above the rest in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country between India and China.

indicators.note: found in says the answer is discovered inside the next word, sitting among its letters

parts.note: the third to fifth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A vehicle discovered in a Central American country.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a motor vehicle, so the answer is an example of the definition.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall hoist on building sites
second meaning: a long-legged, long-necked wading bird

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a machine for hoisting a bird; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hoisting machine with a swinging arm and a tall wading bird the machine is named after.

clue.text: Worst and best part of a motor race?

parts.note: the pits is slang for the very worst
top means best, as in top quality

explanation.surface: Asking which stage of a Grand Prix is the low point and which the high point.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is when a racing car halts in the pits for fuel or tyres, a routine part of a motor race.

indicators.note: partially means only a part is taken, so the answer is a run of letters inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A foolish relative who is something of a family embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means lacking sense or significance, so it is a synonym of silly.

clue.text: Boy eats last of leftover fat

indicators.note: whatever is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A lad finishing off the greasy leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leftover fat' reads as one phrase, but only the last letter of 'leftover' is used and 'fat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is rendered pig fat used in cooking, so it is a kind of fat.

clue.text: Piece from tabloid chaps inserted into broadsheet

indicators.note: inserted into means placed inside, so these pieces go within the outer word

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, is a British broadsheet newspaper
a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A newspaper item picked up by a serious paper from the gutter press.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT (Financial Times) is a serious British daily printed on large broadsheet pages; a rag is a sensational tabloid paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small broken-off part, so it is a synonym of piece.
